figures.claim: 1. Figure 1: Overview of the HNSW topology leakage attack. Given only the layer-0 adjacency list from a leaked HNSW index, the attacker applies degree-penalized geodesic embedding to reconstruct approximate coordinates, enabling recovery of kNN neighborhoods beyond those explicitly present in the leaked graph.
figures.explanation: Analysis stage: Figure 1 is a conceptual pipeline diagram (not a data-driven plot). The code repository fully implements the described pipeline: exp/hnsw_audit/graph/hnsw_builder.py extracts layer-0 adjacency; exp/hnsw_audit/reconstruction/edge_weights.py implements degree-penalized weighting; exp/hnsw_audit/reconstruction/geodesic_reconstruct.py implements geodesic embedding + Landmark MDS; exp/hnsw_audit/evaluation/metrics.py measures kNN recovery. The pipeline description matches the implementation.

results_section.claim: 1. our degree-penalized geodesic method achieves Recall@10 of 0.4164, a 28% relative improvement over the adjacency-only baseline (0.3248)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Both numbers verified: msmarco10k_degree_penalized/RESULTS.json (0.4164) and msmarco10k_adjacency_only/RESULTS.json (0.3248). Relative improvement: 0.4164/0.3248 - 1 = 0.282 = 28.2%, confirmed in effectiveness_evaluation_result.json.

results_section.claim: 2. The degree penalty provides a 52–67% relative improvement over unweighted geodesic (0.2684 vs. 0.1603 on SIFT10K; 0.4164 vs. 0.2731 on MSMARCO-10K)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: All four numbers verified in RESULTS.json files. SIFT: 0.2684/0.1603 - 1 = 67.4%; MSMARCO: 0.4164/0.2731 - 1 = 52.5%. Both within the stated 52-67% range. effectiveness_evaluation_result.json also reports these exact percentages.

results_section.claim: 3. All results are highly consistent across random seeds (standard deviation <0.003 for Recall@10)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Verified across all RESULTS.json files: SIFT adj std=0.0006, SIFT unweighted std=0.001567, SIFT deg-pen std=0.003015 (~0.003, marginal), MSMARCO adj std=0.0007, MSMARCO deg-pen std=0.000339, MSMARCO unweighted std=0.002. All are at or below 0.003.

results_section.claim: 4. α = 1.0 achieves 94% of the best recall (0.1852 vs. 0.1964 at α = 4.0)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Both values verified in hyperparameter_ablation/RESULTS.json. 0.1852/0.1964 = 0.9430 = 94.3%, rounds to 94%. defaults_assessment confirms this.

results_section.claim: 5. L = 256 achieves 93% of the best recall (0.1852 vs. 0.1988 at L = 1024) while requiring only 20% of the computation time (0.84s vs. 4.27s)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: All values verified in hyperparameter_ablation/RESULTS.json. 0.1852/0.1988 = 0.9316 = 93.2%; 0.84/4.27 = 0.197 = 20%. defaults_assessment also confirms both defaults are reasonable.

results_section.claim: 6. the ER graph yields near-chance Recall@10 (0.0013 for adjacency-only, 0.0011 for reconstruction), only 1.3× and 1.1× above the theoretical chance level of 0.001
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: All values verified in sanity_checks/RESULTS.json: er_adjacency_only=0.00129 (rounds to 0.0013), er_degree_penalized=0.00109 (rounds to 0.0011), chance=0.001. Ratios: 0.00129/0.001=1.29≈1.3×; 0.00109/0.001=1.09≈1.1×. er_adj_vs_chance_ratio=1.29 and er_recon_vs_chance_ratio=1.09 are stored in the file.

results_section.claim: 7. the HNSW graph achieves 269× higher recall than the ER baseline
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: Verified: HNSW adj recall = 0.3475 (sift10k_adjacency_only/RESULTS.json), ER adj recall = 0.00129 (sanity_checks/RESULTS.json). 0.3475/0.00129 = 269.4, rounds to 269×.
